nodes.label: Single source-of-truth data layer (src/lib/data)
nodes.rationale: Every artifact (SDKs, MCP, docs, OpenAPI, samples) is regenerated from one data layer so no hand-maintained copy can drift.

nodes.label: bake:all build step
nodes.rationale: packages/*/data/ is generated and gitignored so baked artifacts can never drift from src/ or leak env values into git.

nodes.label: Static pre-rendered HTML with SPA fallback
nodes.rationale: Every known route ships as static HTML; unknown routes fall back to __spa-fallback.html via per-platform catch-all rewrites, and each host reads only its own rewrite file so they cannot conflict.
nodes.norm_label: static pre-rendered html with spa fallback

nodes.label: Backend-only HMAC-SHA256 request signing
nodes.rationale: access_key is a server-side secret; SDKs are backend-only and signing must never happen in a browser.

nodes.label: Admin Config Console v1 (in-browser GitOps editor)
nodes.norm_label: admin config console v1 (in-browser gitops editor)

nodes.label: Edit Flow (Flow A) — propose changes as a PR
nodes.rationale: All edits land as pull requests so code review and deploy previews gate production changes.
nodes.norm_label: edit flow (flow a) — propose changes as a pr

nodes.label: Deploy Flow (Flow B) — dev to main PR
nodes.rationale: The host's git integration builds production on push to main, so no separate deploy GitHub Action exists.
nodes.norm_label: deploy flow (flow b) — dev to main pr

nodes.label: Editable file allowlist + path sanitization
nodes.rationale: Only .md/.mdx under the docs content paths are writable; traversal and control characters are rejected so an admin session cannot rewrite arbitrary repo files.

nodes.label: Persisted admin GitHub token keyed by session id
nodes.rationale: Commits are authored by the admin, not a bot, for accountability; token scoping to a session prevents cross-user misuse and revocation degrades writes only (401 NO_GH_TOKEN), never reads.
nodes.norm_label: persisted admin github token keyed by session id

nodes.label: 409 STALE_CONTENT concurrent-edit guard
nodes.rationale: Backend content differing from the editor's version rejects the write rather than silently clobbering a concurrent edit.

nodes.label: buildAgentBundle (pure deterministic bundle builder)
nodes.rationale: No I/O and no Date, so identical inputs give byte-stable output; dev middleware and prod build call the same builder to eliminate dev/prod drift.

nodes.label: /agent/eps.json canonical agent bundle
nodes.rationale: The bundle is the only intermediate; nothing downstream re-reads api-specs.ts directly.

nodes.label: FNV-1a content-hash bundleVersion
nodes.rationale: Version changes only when topics/apis/recipes content changes, so rebuilds are byte-stable and diffable.

nodes.label: buildInstallMatrix (per-harness MCP wiring)
nodes.rationale: MCP install is recorded the way each harness actually accepts it (CLI command, JSON config, TOML table) — never a bare npx line no harness runs verbatim.

nodes.label: buildContextPackBody (one canonical pack body)
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and copilot-instructions.md share one body; each wrapper only adds a format-appropriate heading.

nodes.label: EPS backend-only auth model (secret-key derivation)
nodes.rationale: secret-key = base64(HMAC-SHA256(timestamp_ms, base64(access_key))); the warning and algorithm are inlined into every context pack so agents cannot get it wrong.

nodes.label: auth topic testVector (dummy key + fixed timestamp)
nodes.rationale: Lets an integrator prove their signing code without anyone handling a real credential — which is why no tool anywhere takes an access_key parameter.
nodes.norm_label: auth topic testvector (dummy key + fixed timestamp)

nodes.label: /ai hub page + /ai.md text twin
nodes.rationale: Both surfaces render from the same buildInstallMatrix() + RECIPES so text and HTML can never diverge.

nodes.label: RecipeStep.branches success-path data gap
nodes.rationale: branches encodes only the exceptional jump (e.g. 463 -> onboard sender); the implied success path has nowhere to live, so neither stepper nor mermaid graph draws it. Fixing means extending the step shape.

nodes.label: eps plugin distribution (marketplace + per-agent install)
nodes.rationale: The transactional MCP is deliberately kept out of the coding marketplace: a developer's coding agent has no partner credentials, so installing it yields MISSING_CREDENTIALS — wrong audience.

nodes.label: AI-native vs AI-friendly distinction
nodes.rationale: Shipping machine-readable artifacts earns 'agent-ready'; 'AI-native' requires agents to act, verify and self-correct with a measured success rate.

nodes.label: Guarded action tools (run_call_in_sandbox, scaffold_integration, validate_signature, run_conformance)
nodes.rationale: MCP is read-only today; adding action tools closes the loop while keeping the backend-only/no-secrets discipline.
nodes.norm_label: guarded action tools (run_call_in_sandbox, scaffold_integration, validate_signature, run_conformance)

nodes.label: Cross-harness agent evals
nodes.rationale: Without evals the AI-native claim is marketing; with them it is true and defensible.

nodes.label: Machine-readable capability manifest
nodes.rationale: Partial rails make an agent hit a gap and lose trust; either complete coverage or publish what the platform can and cannot do so the agent never over-promises.

nodes.label: Live freshness (version + changelog, EPS_BUNDLE_URL remote refresh)
nodes.norm_label: live freshness (version + changelog, eps_bundle_url remote refresh)

nodes.label: Agent governance & safety guardrails
nodes.rationale: Regulated domain: sandbox-vs-prod gating, rate limits, no-secret-leak enforcement must be formalized and made agent-visible.

nodes.label: Master endpoint nomenclature
nodes.rationale: Specs encode the master /customer/payment/<rail>/sender/{customer_id}/... path even where the live API still serves a legacy path mid-migration; the reference slug records live reality.

nodes.label: No-fabrication authoring rule (blocked: source incomplete)
nodes.rationale: For financial/KYC rails a missing reference value blocks the row rather than shipping a half-spec; source URL + fetch date are recorded in sourceDoc.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — helpers, verification extras, BBPS extras
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 — helpers, verification extras, bbps extras

nodes.label: API technical specification layer (api-specs.ts)
nodes.rationale: Kept separate from api-product-pages.ts marketing content so each concern has one home and shared elements are not duplicated.

nodes.label: responseTypes (response_type_id branching)
nodes.rationale: Declared as data rather than a hand-written table in description, so the docs table, OpenAPI description, agent bundle and sample annotations all generate from one field. Meanings are flow-specific so they live per-spec, not in a global registry.

nodes.label: resolveDescription / resolveShortDescription
nodes.rationale: File-first for the docs HTML page, inline-first for text sinks, so one spec can carry a rich descriptionFile and a short inline description without either sink getting the wrong one.

nodes.label: Disable an API (disabled: true, never delete)
nodes.rationale: Filtering once at the API_SPECS export removes the endpoint from every surface with no other edit; the researched data survives and re-enabling is one word. Build guards fail loudly on dangling inbound references because a half-removed endpoint is exactly the drift they exist to catch.
nodes.norm_label: disable an api (disabled: true, never delete)

nodes.label: Spec data provenance caveat
nodes.rationale: Some response shapes were seeded from curated samples rather than live JS-rendered portal pages — treat as best-effort and reconcile against live calls.

nodes.label: Stale-chunk auto-reload
nodes.rationale: A deploy landing between page load and the first click on a lazy route made the SPA rewrite return HTML for a missing chunk, so React.lazy threw and Suspense fallback null blanked the page.

nodes.label: installChunkErrorReload / reloadOnceForStaleChunk
nodes.rationale: A sessionStorage timestamp caps forced reloads at one per 30s so a genuinely broken deploy cannot loop.

nodes.label: /assets/* excluded from SPA-shell rewrite
nodes.rationale: Missing chunks must fail fast with a 404 instead of 200+HTML, which the browser rejects as a MIME-type error.

nodes.label: SEARCH_INDEX auto-generated at module scope
nodes.rationale: Built from the same product/industry/solution data modules, so new APIs, industries and solutions appear in search automatically with no separate index to maintain.

nodes.label: Palette lazy chunk isolation
nodes.rationale: Only the fixed-size trigger pill and a keydown listener live in the main bundle — zero initial-bundle impact and zero CLS; the big data modules are already shared Rollup chunks so referencing them costs no extra network.

nodes.label: Palette SSG safety (never renders during prerender)
nodes.rationale: searchMounted starts false and the index touches no window at module scope, so dist/index.html carries the pill but no cmdk markup.
nodes.norm_label: palette ssg safety (never renders during prerender)

nodes.label: Configuration guide — every knob in one place
nodes.rationale: Edit data/config, never generated output or individual page components.
nodes.norm_label: configuration guide — every knob in one place

nodes.label: FAQ answers are markdown
nodes.rationale: GFM tables and autolinks are deliberately not enabled; internal links client-navigate, everything else opens in a new tab.

nodes.label: stripMarkdown (plain-text sink helper)
nodes.rationale: Centralized for JSON-LD and the command palette so no call site re-introduces its own stripping; it flattens a documented subset only — widen via an AST, not more regexes.

nodes.label: Mutually exclusive FaqTag categories
nodes.rationale: /docs/faqs renders one section per tag, so a second tag would show the same FAQ twice; tests enforce tagging, non-empty sections and single membership.

nodes.label: Per-platform deploy/rewrite configs
nodes.rationale: Each platform reads only its own file so they cannot conflict; /console and /admin are noindexed at three layers.

nodes.label: ConsoleLayout (auth branches + left rail)
nodes.rationale: Owns every auth branch so sub-pages carry no auth logic; borrows DocsLayout's shape outright so console and /docs read as one product, and caps no width because a layout legislating width forces the next wide page to fight it.

nodes.label: WalletBalance card
nodes.rationale: Sits outside <nav> because it is account state, not navigation; renders nothing on 403 rather than an empty card, and stays visible at every width because a balance behind a hamburger is not the always-visible one Eloka has.

nodes.label: Module-scope wallet-balance cache
nodes.rationale: AnimatedRoutes remounts the card on every console navigation, so per-mount state meant a refetch and a Loading flash each hop and a cooldown a user could walk past. Only settled answers cache; AuthProvider clears it whenever the session goes anon so the next signer-in cannot see the previous balance.

nodes.label: GET /wallet/balance BFF route (interaction 9)
nodes.rationale: Identity is re-derived from the session claim's mobile via the 151 profile on every call, never read from the request, so one developer cannot read another's wallet. 403 (ineligible) and 502 (upstream failure) stay distinct so a transient failure never permanently retires a real balance.

nodes.label: My Profile page (/console/profile)
nodes.rationale: Issues no request of its own — reads the MeView the layout already fetched. Profile completeness uses onboarding progress rather than Eloka's field checklist, whose own count treats an absent key as complete.

nodes.label: PROFILE_DETAIL_BLOCKS allowlist
nodes.rationale: An allowlist, not a passthrough: whatever lands there is readable by anything running in the page, so a block upstream adds later must be reviewed before it ships.

nodes.label: sessionStorage /me session cache
nodes.rationale: Hydrated in an effect, never in the useState initializer, because prerendered HTML is built with status loading and a synchronous read would trip a hydration mismatch. Display data only — every request still carries the session cookie.

nodes.label: API keys management (blocked on issuance contract)
nodes.rationale: The core reason a developer logs in, but blocked on the Eko credential-issuance API contract; the Credentials page ships a production empty state with no request button until it lands.
nodes.norm_label: api keys management (blocked on issuance contract)

nodes.label: Console sandbox / API playground (planned)
nodes.rationale: Today it lives only in /docs behind a CORS proxy; the console should own it, pre-authenticated with the developer's UAT key.

nodes.label: Developer docs portal (/docs)
nodes.rationale: Spec-driven: no endpoint detail, parameter table or code snippet is hand-authored per endpoint — all are derived at read time from typed data.

nodes.label: EndpointDetail (centre pane)
nodes.rationale: Reads through the resolvers, never raw spec fields, so common params and auth headers appear without being declared per-spec.

nodes.label: sampleFor (language dispatch)
nodes.rationale: Samples are generated on demand from the spec, never stored statically, so they cannot drift.

nodes.label: HEADER_PLACEHOLDER (secrets never emitted)
nodes.rationale: Computed/signed header values render as obvious placeholder tokens; only the live Try-it console substitutes real locally-signed values, guarded by a placeholder-leak test.

nodes.label: DocsLayout 3-pane grid
nodes.rationale: Nav tree and theme toggle are injected as props/children rather than hard-wired, so guides render without a right pane and endpoints render with one.

nodes.label: ROUTE_CHUNK_MAP modulepreload
nodes.rationale: Lets the prerenderer preload the right page module per route, avoiding a bundle-to-chunk waterfall.

nodes.label: Docs-local dark theme (scoped .dark)
nodes.rationale: The .dark class is applied to the DocsLayout root, not <html>, so the rest of the site stays light; the server renders light mode and the client applies the saved theme after mount to avoid a hydration mismatch.

nodes.label: @theme inline requirement
nodes.rationale: Load-bearing: it keeps semantic --color-* bindings live at use-site; without inline, Tailwind would bake the :root value at build time and the scoped .dark class would have no effect.

nodes.label: Globally themed scrollbars
nodes.rationale: One declaration on --foreground tracks both themes; the WebKit pseudo-element block is gated behind @supports not (scrollbar-color: auto) so browsers supporting both do not style twice.

nodes.label: GUIDES metadata registry (docs-guides.ts)
nodes.rationale: Metadata is split from components and kept free of .mdx imports (and of YAML frontmatter) so Node, SSG route enumeration and tests can read guide metadata without the MDX toolchain.

nodes.label: GUIDE_COMPONENTS registry (eager imports)
nodes.rationale: Imports are eager, not lazy, so server and client render the same tree during hydration.

nodes.label: SecretKeyTester (in-browser signing playground)
nodes.rationale: Computes and verifies the HMAC in the browser with Web Crypto so the access key never leaves the page; SSR-safe because the timestamp is seeded from a mount effect.

nodes.label: renderGuideMarkdown (markdown twin of guides)
nodes.rationale: Every custom MDX tag must have a substitution; unhandled forms throw at build time rather than leaking raw JSX into /docs/<slug>.md.

nodes.label: docs-registry.ts (guides + endpoints unifier)
nodes.rationale: Imports no React and no .mdx so ssg/routes.ts and unit tests can load it; URL model, slug guard, left menu and prerender list all come out of this one file.

nodes.label: Flat /docs/<slug> URL model
nodes.rationale: The HTTP method is kept out of the URL and surfaced via nav/detail method tags instead; guides and endpoints share one namespace.

nodes.label: assertNoSlugCollisions (module-load guard)
nodes.rationale: Runs at module load and throws on duplicate or reserved slugs, so a bad slug fails the build and the tests rather than production.

nodes.label: DocsNavTree (single-endpoint flattening)
nodes.rationale: A product with exactly one endpoint skips its sub-heading to avoid redundant 'Passport Verification > Passport Verification' nesting.

nodes.label: -status spec convention (docs-visible, marketing-hidden)
nodes.rationale: Async-job pollers are real endpoints and stay in the docs; they are hidden only on product detail pages and the product .md tree so marketing is not cluttered with each bulk API's status companion.

nodes.label: Declare once, recompose at read time
nodes.rationale: One edit to COMMON_REQUEST_PARAMS updates every param table, every code sample and every generated .md; ApiProductId is a literal union so a productId typo fails the build.
nodes.norm_label: declare once, recompose at read time

nodes.label: resolveHeaders
nodes.rationale: content-type is derived per endpoint (multipart when any type:"file" body param exists) and the SDKs apply the same rule at runtime.

nodes.label: resolveRequestParams
nodes.rationale: Common params declare allowedMethods instead of a fixed 'in', so location is derived from the method (GET -> query, else body) and write-only params drop off GETs.

nodes.label: Scalar "Try it" console
nodes.rationale: Replaced a hand-rolled TryItPanel that did a direct fetch and hit CORS; the lower-level createApiClientModal is used because the React wrapper does not forward plugins and the client does not run x-pre-request scripts.

nodes.label: ekoSigningPlugin (beforeRequest hook)
nodes.rationale: Runs after auth schemes populate headers and immediately before the request is built, so deleting access_key is deterministic — only the derived signature leaves the browser.

nodes.label: tryit-client.ts (client-only Scalar modal singleton)
nodes.rationale: Loaded only via a dynamic import inside useTryIt's callback so the Vue app and the 342 KB spec layer stay out of the server module graph and the initial docs bundle.

nodes.label: Interactive OpenAPI document ({ interactive: true })
nodes.rationale: The public openapi.json stays pristine and byte-stable; only the modal's variant adds apiKey security schemes and drops the signing headers the schemes and plugin supply.

nodes.label: Try-it CORS proxy (VITE_SCALAR_PROXY_URL)
nodes.rationale: Honest framing: with the hosted proxy the developer_key, computed secret-key and bodies transit a third party — acceptable for sandbox traffic, and the raw access_key is never transmitted. Blank the var for zero third-party transit.

nodes.label: DEV-only credential prefill
nodes.rationale: Gated by import.meta.env.DEV, which is false during the Node prerender and in production, so credentials never reach static output.

nodes.label: EPS transactional MCP server
nodes.rationale: Executes verification APIs with the partner's own credentials for their production agents — deliberately not a coding-agent plugin and absent from the marketplace.

nodes.label: Tool generation from the baked bundle (src/tools.ts)
nodes.rationale: Filters to verification and non-financial specs and emits one eps_<slug> tool each; editing api-specs.ts and rebuilding is all it takes to add a tool, and a startup assertion fails the build if a spec needs a header the executor cannot send.
nodes.norm_label: tool generation from the baked bundle (src/tools.ts)

nodes.label: Pass-through credential custody
nodes.rationale: Keys arrive as per-request headers, sign, and vanish with the request — nothing in KV or on disk, so leak blast radius is one request in memory.

nodes.label: sanitizeError (PII-safe error curation)
nodes.rationale: Upstream/network error text can echo request data (PAN/Aadhaar/bank), so it is replaced; only EpsClient validation messages naming params pass through, and the access log carries the tool name only.

nodes.label: X-Eko-Allowed-Apis tool scoping
nodes.rationale: Voluntary scoping, not entitlement: it lives in partner-controlled client config out of the model's reach, but the Eko credentials remain the true authz boundary.

nodes.label: In-memory abuse throttling
nodes.rationale: Best-effort fixed window (60/10min) keyed on env + hashed developer key; per-process and reset on restart — move to shared Redis KV if this ever runs multi-instance.

nodes.label: Stateless streamable HTTP transport
nodes.rationale: A fresh transport per POST with no sessions and no GET/SSE stream (405, spec-legal), so initialize, tools/list and tools/call each stand alone.

nodes.label: Local stdio transport + startup update check
nodes.rationale: Only the stdio bin does the npm latest check — remote users cannot self-update and stderr there is operator log noise.
nodes.norm_label: local stdio transport + startup update check

nodes.label: Separate container from eps-backend
nodes.rationale: eps-backend holds admin GitHub OAuth tokens with GitOps deploy rights; compose co-location is ops convenience, the container is the security boundary.

nodes.label: Path-namespaced nginx reverse proxy (/transact/, /context/ reserved)
nodes.rationale: A trailing-slash proxy_pass strips the prefix so the app serves bare /mcp unchanged (safe because the transport emits no absolute URLs); the proxy must overwrite x-real-ip for the rate-limit fallback and disable request and response buffering.

nodes.label: Auto-pull poller (image digest watcher)
nodes.rationale: Retagging :prod on every green main plus a poller that recreates the service on a digest change makes 'update the tools' mean 'merge the spec change'; a distinct volume keeps its lock/HOLD state separate from the backend's.

nodes.label: Gated UAT smoke test (base URL + auth proof)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed the portless environment URLs sign end-to-end; a failure means fixing meta.environments in the SSOT, never patching URLs in this package.
nodes.norm_label: gated uat smoke test (base url + auth proof)

nodes.label: Docker vfs storage-driver trap
nodes.rationale: Under vfs every layer is copied in full, so an auto-redeploying stack fills the disk; the tell is 'no space left on device' while df shows free space. Switching to overlay2 orphans existing images, so save them first.

nodes.label: parity.sdk-surface test (eps.json vs sdk-surface skew guard)
nodes.norm_label: parity.sdk-surface test (eps.json vs sdk-surface skew guard)

nodes.label: VITE_SHOW_TRANSACT_MCP marketing gate
nodes.rationale: The /agents page, nav split, prerender, sitemap and llms.txt entry appear only once the flag is on — flip it only after production deploy and smoke test.

nodes.label: Business Dashboard (/console)
nodes.rationale: Total Transactions is the headline because an EPS partner is billed per API call; Eloka leads with GTV because its users move other people's money for commission — the inverse business.

nodes.label: One requestPayload key per call
nodes.rationale: A multi-key payload had upstream silently omit two datasets — two blank widgets on a healthy account with no error anywhere. The four calls run concurrently so wall-clock is the slowest, not the sum.

nodes.label: pickDataset (exact-before-normalized key matching)
nodes.rationale: Upstream naming is inconsistent (three of four datasets snake-to-camel, one does not), so exact candidates are tried before normalized ones and an ambiguous normalized match resolves to nothing rather than to whichever key serialized first.

nodes.label: buildDashboardView (upstream normalizer)
nodes.rationale: Downline-only widgets are dropped at the backend boundary so they never reach the browser; any block may arrive JSON-encoded so everything goes through one decode, and a service map arriving as an array is rejected rather than rendering 'Service 0' nonsense.

nodes.label: Server-side IST date-window maths
nodes.rationale: The backend runs UTC but Eko's data is stamped IST, so computing 'today' in UTC would open a Delhi partner's window 5h30m late; the browser sends only a preset because an arbitrary window is an unbounded upstream scan.

nodes.label: Dashboard caching (scoped keys, closed-window TTL)
nodes.rationale: Windows other than today end at yesterday 23:59:59 — closed windows whose numbers cannot change — so they hold 900s. The scope hash prevents a shared Redis from serving UAT numbers to a live partner, and an empty service list is never cached.

nodes.label: Zero versus absent (shape logging)
nodes.rationale: A quiet week and an out-of-scope account both look like zeros, so zeros are never hidden and the route logs raw= (what each dry call actually received) — without it an upstream answering under an unasked-for name would be invisible. shapeOf reports keys and kinds only, never a partner's values.

nodes.label: Service filter (narrowed 1044 master list)
nodes.rationale: Options are recomputed only from an unfiltered view, or a filtered response would collapse the dropdown to the current selection; it resets on window change and is a native <select> rather than 150 lines of Radix that does not exist yet.

nodes.label: Most Used Services falls back to Success Rates
nodes.rationale: An approximation, not a second source of truth: if upstream ever scopes the two blocks differently the counts drift. Delete it once mostUsedServices is reliable.
nodes.norm_label: most used services falls back to success rates

nodes.label: React.lazy recharts widgets
nodes.rationale: AppServer imports ConsoleHome eagerly for the static build, so a plain import would drag ~250KB of charting into the SSG bundle; each chart also renders a text summary because an SVG is invisible to a screen reader and jsdom measures zero.

nodes.label: Dashboard degradation ladder (501/401/502)
nodes.rationale: Mounted unconditionally and answering a named 501 lets the console say 'not on this deployment' instead of guessing at a 404; a failing 1044 is non-fatal because refusing the filter would turn a cosmetic outage into a broken one.

nodes.label: GET /connect/token endpoint
nodes.rationale: The widget reads sessionStorage in the host realm and has no token prop or postMessage API, while this app's session is an HttpOnly cookie — so supporting it required deliberately publishing an upstream credential to the browser. /connect/* is mounted only when CONNECT_API_BASE_URL is set.

nodes.label: access_token_lite exposure trade-off
nodes.rationale: Setting the lite token means the widget's full-token fallback never fires, so the full access token and refresh token stay server-side; the two exposed tokens are XSS-readable only while a flow is on screen and are cleared on unmount, sign-out and expiry.

nodes.label: Tokens written before the runtime loads
nodes.rationale: The widget starts calling connect-api the moment it upgrades; a request that beats the token into storage goes out as Bearer null.
nodes.norm_label: tokens written before the runtime loads

nodes.label: Server-side support-ticket assembly
nodes.rationale: Zoho-Desk formatting lives server-side so the console never learns the ticket schema and cannot claim to be a different user; caps on attachments, fields and free text are enforced at the trust boundary, the browser check being only a courtesy.

nodes.label: ConnectDialogProvider (promise-per-dialog stack)
nodes.rationale: Replaces Eloka's 571-line pub/sub loader, whose indirection existed only because it was mounted in a Next.js layout that could not see its callers; every dialog is React.lazy so webcam/crop/MediaPipe stay out of the initial bundle.

nodes.label: <FileUpload> control
nodes.rationale: Every image routes through the editor before the caller sees it, so a form receives a cropped, size-capped JPEG instead of a 4 MB photo of a desk.

nodes.label: Watermark provenance stamping
nodes.rationale: A KYC photo is evidence and evidence without provenance can be re-used for another customer; coordinates can be spoofed on a rooted phone while an observed IP cannot, so the line carries both, resolved on mount so a late prompt cannot stamp a blank location.

nodes.label: syncWidgetProps (React 19 property gotcha)
nodes.rationale: React 19 assigns properties on an upgraded custom element where older React set attributes, and Polymer only JSON-parses attributes — so real objects are assigned via a ref, with interaction_id last because it is the observed property that starts the flow.

nodes.label: id vs interaction_type_id
nodes.rationale: interaction_type_id is 0 for every composite interaction, so keying role_trxn_list by type collapses them all onto "0" and entitlement lookup finds nothing; rows are passed through whole because the widget reads behavior, group_interaction_ids, icon and uri too.

nodes.label: connect-api CORS allowlist blocker
nodes.rationale: Every widget request is cross-origin and cannot be fixed from this repo, so VITE_SHOW_CONNECT_WIDGET stays false until connect-api allowlists the console origin.

nodes.label: /console/test DEV dialog bench
nodes.rationale: Dialogs are hard to reach through a real flow, so a DEV-only bench opens each directly; route and rail item sit behind import.meta.env.DEV with the import inside the guard so no chunk ships in production.

nodes.label: descriptionFile endpoint notes (src/content/docs/endpoints/*.md)
nodes.rationale: Long/rich descriptions live as real markdown files to keep api-specs.ts lean; MDX is excluded from that folder so the files load as raw text, not compiled components.

nodes.label: KYC Document Upload (/console/documents)
nodes.rationale: Onboarding creates the account; KYC activates it. Moves the identity/business document pack from email into the console.

nodes.label: connect-api interaction 586 — fetch required document list
nodes.rationale: Keyed by `id` (not interaction_type_id) in buildRoleTransactionList because every composite interaction reports interaction_type_id: 0.
nodes.norm_label: connect-api interaction 586 — fetch required document list

nodes.label: connect-api interaction 587 — upload one document (multipart)
nodes.rationale: Every field travels URL-encoded inside a single `formdata` part; files are sibling parts file1..fileN — connect-api's own convention, not general multipart.

nodes.label: uploadInteraction (shared multipart transport)
nodes.rationale: Support-ticket attachments already use this transport, so KYC upload reuses one helper instead of a second multipart implementation.

nodes.label: KYC_NO_RECORDS — "No Records Found" is an empty state
nodes.rationale: Upstream returns a failed envelope for an account with nothing outstanding; matching the message renders a reassuring empty state instead of a red error. Message-matching is all upstream gives; prefer a response_type_id if one ever surfaces.
nodes.norm_label: kyc_no_records — "no records found" is an empty state

nodes.label: kycEnabled / useKycEnabled entitlement gate
nodes.rationale: Requires BOTH 586 and 587 — listing without uploading renders a page whose every button fails upstream. Returns null while unresolved so callers distinguish 'not entitled' from 'not yet loaded'. Two independent guards (rail item + page) because a nav item is not access control.

nodes.label: parseDocumentList (presentation overlay, drops is_required)
nodes.rationale: is_required is deliberately not carried across — an incomplete pack fails at review days later, so offering 'optional' is offering a slow way to fail.

nodes.label: KYC_DOC_CONFIG — per-doc_type local overrides
nodes.rationale: Upstream's list is shared across Eko products and says nothing about how a document should be captured. Local always wins (`??` merge); an unknown doc_type gets an empty config, never an error.

nodes.label: Watermark provenance stamp (opt-in per doc_type)
nodes.rationale: Only doc_type "24" (live photograph) asks: a stamp is evidence about a capture this console witnessed; on a scan of a pre-existing card it defaces the document and proves nothing. Images only; never combine with options.disableImageConfirm.

nodes.label: Sample documents (sampleUrl blanks in public/kyc-samples)
nodes.rationale: For documents whose wording is Eko's to dictate (board resolution, declarations). Files are committed so a revision is a reviewable diff; kyc-docs.test.ts pins the path shape and on-disk existence so a rename fails CI instead of 404-ing.

nodes.label: DOCUMENT_STATUS / statusOfDocument (1 pending, 2 success, 3 resubmit)
nodes.rationale: Unknown codes are treated as not-yet-uploaded, never a false 'done'. `uploadedNow` bridges the gap between an upload and a refetch that may not yet reflect it.

nodes.label: KYC file rules (KYC_TYPES, KYC_EXTENSIONS, KYC_MAX_FILE_BYTES, KYC_MAX_PAGES)
nodes.rationale: Explicit type list rather than image/* — the wildcard admits HEIC, WEBP and SVG (a script carrier). MIME AND extension must both pass because the browser supplies both and either alone is trivially wrong. KYC takes 10 MB where a ticket attachment takes 5; backend copy is authority.
nodes.norm_label: kyc file rules (kyc_types, kyc_extensions, kyc_max_file_bytes, kyc_max_pages)

nodes.label: KycUploadDialog
nodes.rationale: Plain shadcn Dialog, deliberately not a DialogHost entry, so camera/editor/viewer portals stack above it on their own. On failure it stays open with files attached — re-picking pages after a network blip is the worst recovery.

nodes.label: ignoreNestedDialogInteraction (Radix top-layer guard)
nodes.rationale: Radix defers its top-layer test to the click after pointerdown; the upper dialog unmounts during that click so the lower one reads as topmost and dismisses itself. Not reproducible under jsdom — checked by hand at /console/test.

nodes.label: `multiple` — per-slot attachments combined into one PDF
nodes.rationale: A phone rarely gets a whole Aadhaar card square in one frame. Per slot, not per document; a single attachment passes through unchanged so nothing becomes a PDF that did not need to be.
nodes.norm_label: `multiple` — per-slot attachments combined into one pdf

nodes.label: Transaction History (/console/transactions)
nodes.rationale: Ported from Eloka's History feature; columns are literal JSX and logic is plain functions because Eloka's 918-line historyParametersMetadata engine exists to serve views this page does not have.

nodes.label: Interaction 154 — transaction history upstream
nodes.rationale: Runs on its own host/port and an older API version — not the main upstream. Each URL part is an optional override falling back to the main upstream.

nodes.label: debitOf / creditOf money rules
nodes.rationale: Return 0 not "" — blanking an empty cell is the renderer's job; Eloka folds blanking into compute and then coerces numbers back out of strings downstream. A failed row (response_status_id 1) contributes 0 to both.

nodes.label: inferSearchField (quick-search shape heuristic)
nodes.rationale: The ranges overlap (a 10-digit input is both a valid mobile and a valid TID), so the order of the checks IS the spec — pinned by a boundary table test.

nodes.label: selectEvalueAccountId (E-value account resolution)
nodes.rationale: Omitting account_id makes upstream fall back to the default account — quietly reporting somebody else's history. Refusing with 502 NO_ACCOUNT is the honest answer. Negative synthetic ids (-500000 'Response Awaited') are always filtered out.

nodes.label: parseFilters allow-list (trust boundary)
nodes.rationale: Only known keys are copied out and shape-checked so no extra interaction field (org_id, interaction_type_id) can be smuggled upstream. Mirrors parseBusiness in signup.ts.

nodes.label: POST /transactions/search (POST, not GET)
nodes.rationale: Filters carry mobile numbers, account numbers, TIDs and amounts; a query string would put all of them into browser history, proxy logs, and this app's own access log.

nodes.label: SIMPLIBANK_HISTORY_* upstream override (eko.historyUrl)
nodes.rationale: Per-part overrides falling back to the main upstream so a deployment sharing one box only has to set the path; the history host runs the same plaintext-http guard.

nodes.label: Per-page totals / Closing Balance caveat
nodes.rationale: Upstream returns no grand totals, so the footer sums only on-screen rows and is labelled 'Totals for this page'. Real totals are an API change, not a UI one.

nodes.label: transactions.sample.ts (captured interaction-154 response)
nodes.rationale: A genuine captured response settles envelope shape, string coercions, absent amount fields, ISO-8601 +05:30 datetimes and pre-masked mobiles/accounts; mapTransactionRows is tested against it.

nodes.label: Self-serve signup wizard (/signup)
nodes.rationale: OTP → partial account → PAN → Business Details → PIN → /console, replacing the old Zoho lead-capture iframe. Every step re-fetches interaction 151 so resume-after-drop-off and retry-after-failure are the same code path.

nodes.label: `onboarding === 1` classification gate in getProfile
nodes.rationale: user_type flips to "23" the moment the partial account exists, so it cannot distinguish in-progress from finished. Checking user_type first would classify every mid-onboarding user as not_allowed and permanently lock them out of resuming.

nodes.label: `signup` session role
nodes.rationale: GET /me special-cases the role before any Eko call because AuthProvider boots exclusively from /me — rejecting a signup session would drop a mid-onboarding reload to anon and force a fresh OTP.

nodes.label: respond() signup→developer session upgrade
nodes.rationale: Gates on profile.kind === 'found' rather than buildMeView output, which never throws and would silently mint a developer session for exactly the profiles /auth/otp/verify refuses. A throwing re-fetch still returns done and retries on the next /signup/state.

nodes.label: Pintwin PIN encoding (170 → 10005 → 5)
nodes.rationale: Digit substitution, not encryption — the key ships in the clear, so obfuscation is all it buys alone. The real property is that each key is single-use and invalidated upstream per attempt, so a captured okekey cannot be replayed. Encoding runs entirely in the BFF.

nodes.label: Interaction 521 — createPartialAccount
nodes.rationale: Uses base() — the configured default initiator_id/user_code pair — because no real user identity exists yet, mirroring connect-api's DEFAULT_TRXN_* fallback.

nodes.label: Interaction 523 — verifyPan (multipart)
nodes.rationale: The only onboarding interaction sent as multipart: one part literally named `form-data` carrying the same URL-encoded field string, no file part. Unverified against real upstream — a UAT gate.

nodes.label: Interaction 522 — submitBusiness / BUSINESS_FIELDS
nodes.rationale: The ten field names are unverified against real upstream — every test only asserts our own assumptions back to us; a response_type_id other than 1567 with a field-specific message means a key name is wrong.

nodes.label: ekoLog redaction (first_okekey/second_okekey/pintwin_key)
nodes.rationale: The substitution is a plain digit map, so an okekey AND the pintwin_key that produced it, logged together, recover the PIN exactly — redacting both independently closes this regardless of which log line is read first. Redaction lives inside ekoLog, not at call sites.

nodes.label: INDIAN_STATES (probed from interaction 387)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed against real UAT; its quirks ("PondiCherry" casing, Delhi with a (UT) suffix, "Andhra Pradesh (New)" sorted last, no Ladakh) are load-bearing because interaction 522 matches on the exact string.

nodes.label: ONBOARDING_LATLONG constant
nodes.rationale: This flow does not port Eloka's geolocation capture; Eloka itself falls back to this exact value when capture is skipped or denied. Not confirmed against real UAT.

nodes.label: resolveSteps() + SIGNUP_STEPS registry
nodes.rationale: Step order and labels come from the API's onboarding_steps at runtime; the wizard never branches on step names and each StepDefinition owns its own submit closure. Unknown API roles are silently skipped so the backend can ship a step before the frontend has UI.

nodes.label: StepRail progress UI
nodes.rationale: One component and one DOM tree with orientation swapped in CSS only, so no second render branch can drift; holds no state and returns null rather than claiming 'Step 0 of 0'.

nodes.label: connect-api login delegation (CONNECT_API_BASE_URL)
nodes.rationale: When set, login is delegated to Eloka's connect-api so the EPS portal and Eloka share one identity; mapConnectLogin maps its envelope onto the same ProfileResult union in the same branch order. Only login is delegated.

nodes.label: No Eko access token (developer_key + initiator_id = mobile)
nodes.rationale: The Bearer token Eloka sends never goes upstream — connect-api only derives initiator_id/user_code/org_id from it. initiator_id is the registered mobile, never an internal id; sending ekoUserId earns a misleading 'Invalid Sender/Initiator' 403.
nodes.norm_label: no eko access token (developer_key + initiator_id = mobile)

nodes.label: Two-axis Industries × Packs architecture
nodes.rationale: Every Pack belongs to ≥1 Industry and every Industry uses ≥1 Pack, creating a dense internal-link graph for SEO and letting visitors navigate from 'I am X' to 'I need Y'.

nodes.label: /industries/<slug> and /solutions/<slug> URL structure
nodes.rationale: "Solutions" over "/packs/" because it is a higher-intent search term matching B2B SaaS convention (Razorpay, Cashfree, Setu); "Pack" stays as the on-page brand.

nodes.label: Industry detail page template
nodes.rationale: A visitor arriving from search must immediately see (a) we serve you, (b) the exact recommended bundle, (c) what peers build, (d) how to start. 'Recommended solution packs' is the most important section — it bridges Industry → Pack → API.

nodes.label: Solution/Pack detail page template
nodes.rationale: Answers what's in the box, the job it does, the commercial model, and which industries use it — the 'what's inside the pack' rows explain why each API is present, not just what it does.

nodes.label: Cross-linking model (Industry ↔ Pack ↔ Product)
nodes.rationale: Dense internal linking is what makes the two-axis structure pay off for SEO; product pages gain 'Solutions that include this API' and 'Industries that use this API' sections.

nodes.label: Per-page SEO essentials (JSON-LD FAQPage, OG, canonical)
nodes.rationale: FAQPage structured data frequently triggers rich results and is called out as one of the highest-ROI SEO additions.
nodes.norm_label: per-page seo essentials (json-ld faqpage, og, canonical)

nodes.label: Phased rollout (Foundation → Tier-1/2/3 → Optimization)
nodes.rationale: 11 Tier-1 launch pages are enough to be substantively useful for SEO and sales without waiting for all 17 industries + 26 packs.

nodes.label: Assisted Banking Agent Pack (AePS + DMT + BBPS + PPI)
nodes.rationale: Turns a retail counter into a micro-ATM; bundles the services that serve the 200–300M Indians who can't use UPI or mobile banking.
nodes.norm_label: assisted banking agent pack (aeps + dmt + bbps + ppi)

nodes.label: Removed redundant Payments / UPI Payout API specs (backup)
nodes.rationale: Archive of spec entries deleted from src/lib/data/api-spec.ts, kept verbatim so they can be restored if the removal proves wrong.
nodes.norm_label: removed redundant payments / upi payout api specs (backup)

nodes.label: upi-payout-vpa-verify spec (pre-payout VPA validation)
nodes.rationale: Confirms the NPCI-verified payee name before funds move — eliminates wrong-payee failures and satisfies RBI beneficiary-confirmation.

nodes.label: setup-callback-url spec (payout webhook)
nodes.rationale: Registered instead of polling for NEFT, which may take minutes to confirm; only static URL structures are supported.

nodes.label: AI-Native Agent Platform (feature/ai-native-agent-platform)
nodes.rationale: Status/handover report: 4 phases shipped, everything auto-generated from api-specs.ts; the repo became an npm-workspaces monorepo.

nodes.label: /agent/eps.json canonical bundle (Phase 0 spine)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic (FNV-1a content hash, no Date) so downstream artifacts never re-read the source of truth; every artifact consumes the bundle instead.

nodes.label: @ekoindia/eps-context-mcp (local stdio MCP, 9 tiered tools)
nodes.rationale: Local rather than hosted because EPS only needs its own small static specs — zero hosting, zero secrets, zero ops. Named eps-context-mcp so `eps-mcp` stays reserved for a transactional server; tools are tiered so the agent fetches one API/topic, not the whole docs.

nodes.label: Backend-only signed SDKs (@ekoindia/eps-sdk, ekoindia/eps-sdk PHP)
nodes.rationale: Backend-only by design — secret-key/secret-key-timestamp must never be generated in a frontend app, so access_key is never exposed. HMAC baked in is what generic OpenAPI codegen gets wrong.

nodes.label: @ekoindia/eps-mock-server (offline, recipe-aware)
nodes.rationale: Replays /agent/fixtures.json on :4010 so agents can develop and be evaluated without live calls; scenarios selected via ?eps_scenario=.

nodes.label: packages/claude-plugin-eps (MCP + skills + /eps command)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code installs plugins from a marketplace git repo, so the plugin needs .claude-plugin/marketplace.json hosted and the MCP published before /plugin install works.

nodes.label: Distribution decision: public npm + Packagist
nodes.rationale: The whole value proposition is one-command adoption; public registries deliver that. Monorepo stays, but Packagist reads composer.json from a repo root so the PHP SDK needs a subtree-split mirror.

nodes.label: GitHub Packages rejected for public distribution
nodes.rationale: npm from GitHub Packages requires consumer-side auth + scoped .npmrc even for public installs, so `npx -y @ekoindia/eps-context-mcp` would not just work; and there is no Composer or Go module support at all.
nodes.norm_label: github packages rejected for public distribution

nodes.label: /agents → /ai route rename + marketing redesign
nodes.rationale: The old page rendered inside LegalPageLayout (a v1 shortcut) and read as an unstyled index — functionally complete but useless as an adoption surface. Redesigned as a dedicated hero/install-matrix/artifact-grid page; /ai.md stays as the lean text twin.

nodes.label: Drop-in agent context packs (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, copilot-instructions.md)
nodes.rationale: Generated from one canonical body so every harness gets the same HMAC-signing guidance; ships in days and works in every harness that exists today.
nodes.norm_label: drop-in agent context packs (agents.md, claude.md, .cursorrules, copilot-instructions.md)

nodes.label: API sample-response reconciliation (before/after review)
nodes.rationale: sampleSuccessResponse and responseData both feed code samples, .md twins, the agent bundle, fixtures and OpenAPI — so they must agree and are rewritten together per endpoint.

nodes.label: Hard rule: adopt shape, never live values
nodes.rationale: The source sheet holds real customer/prod data, so only key names, response_type_id and envelope are adopted; every value is reused or replaced with an obviously-fake placeholder, with a grep scan proving zero live values landed.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: adopt shape, never live values

nodes.label: Bucket A — REPLACE (39 endpoints rewritten from prod shape)
nodes.norm_label: bucket a — replace (39 endpoints rewritten from prod shape)

nodes.label: Bucket B — KEEP + FLAG (suspect prod captures)
nodes.rationale: Captures that are timeouts, empty-list cases, mis-harvested rows or a KYC gate rather than the real endpoint response — flagged with TODO(reconcile) instead of overwriting a correct sample with a wrong one.
nodes.norm_label: bucket b — keep + flag (suspect prod captures)

nodes.label: responseData type-inference rules
nodes.rationale: Never infer from a single value blindly: Eko returns most numbers as quoted strings, nulls/empties stay strings, empty containers are described not fabricated, and unknown semantics get 'Returned by the API.' rather than invented behavior.

nodes.label: Sample↔schema parity automated check
nodes.rationale: Asserts sampleSuccessResponse.data keys match resolveResponseFields output and the generated OpenAPI example matches its response schema — catches drift across all bucket-A slugs at once.

nodes.label: eps-transact-mcp VM deployment runbook
nodes.rationale: Deployed to /data/eps-mcp on a SHARED Azure RHEL prod box that also runs the ems container and connect.eko.in nginx; service binds 127.0.0.1:8788 only and is never exposed directly.

nodes.label: mcp.eko.in path namespace contract (/transact/, /context/ reserved)
nodes.rationale: Permanent path-namespacing so a future edge-hosted eps-context-mcp can live at /context/mcp; bare / returns 404 to keep the namespace reserved.

nodes.label: nginx reverse-proxy config (X-Real-IP, no buffering, TLS)
nodes.rationale: X-Real-IP MUST be overwritten because the rate-limit IP fallback trusts it; buffering is off both directions for streamable HTTP; the trailing slash on proxy_pass strips the /transact/ prefix, safe only because the app emits no absolute URLs or redirects.
nodes.norm_label: nginx reverse-proxy config (x-real-ip, no buffering, tls)

nodes.label: GHCR authentication (private images, .ghcr-auth.json)
nodes.rationale: The 'public poller image' claim in the old doc was wrong — images are private. The host daemon needs docker login AND the poller separately needs its own .ghcr-auth.json for skopeo digest checks.

nodes.label: Docker data-root on /data pinned to the vfs driver
nodes.rationale: A fresh /data/docker on ext4 made Docker auto-pick overlay2 and ignore the rsynced vfs data, making ems vanish; pinning storage-driver: vfs recovers it and avoids recreating ems's unscripted docker run config. vfs is slow and bloats, so a weekly image prune cron was added.
nodes.norm_label: docker data-root on /data pinned to the vfs driver

nodes.label: GHCR digest poller auto-deploy with health gate + rollback
nodes.rationale: Polls the :prod digest, pulls on change, rewrites the deploy.env pin, recreates the service, gates on /healthz, and auto-rolls-back to last-good with a HOLD state to stop flapping. Requires Compose v2 at runtime because it shells out to `docker compose`.
nodes.norm_label: ghcr digest poller auto-deploy with health gate + rollback

nodes.label: Certbot renewal timer gotcha
nodes.rationale: After `certbot --nginx` no renewal timer existed and had to be enabled explicitly; a failing dry-run was a transient network blip, not an nginx/redirect problem. Firewalld ports must be verified as permanent, not just runtime.

nodes.label: EPS strategic buy-in deck plan
nodes.rationale: Audience already knows the product, so the time goes on the strategic shift, why now, and shipped proof — leadership respects 'already done' over 'we could'.

nodes.label: Agent-ready (today) vs AI-native (target rung)
nodes.rationale: Owning the honest label pre-empts the obvious challenge and turns the ask into 'fund the 4 steps that earn it' — act, verify, prove (evals), publish.

nodes.label: Thesis: one source of truth → everything regenerates in sync
nodes.rationale: Describe each API once; the build emits SDKs, MCP, OpenAPI, Postman, context packs, mock fixtures and docs — zero drift, zero duplicated maintenance, which also mitigates the maintenance-load risk.
nodes.norm_label: thesis: one source of truth → everything regenerates in sync

nodes.label: Sample UIDAI RD-service integration testing tool (HTML)
nodes.rationale: Standalone jQuery/Bootstrap page that talks to a locally installed Aadhaar biometric RD service over custom HTTP verbs on 127.0.0.1 — the reference for how a browser reaches a fingerprint device.
nodes.norm_label: sample uidai rd-service integration testing tool (html)

nodes.label: discoverAvdm() — RDSERVICE port scan 11100–11112
nodes.rationale: The RD service registers on an unpredictable local port, so discovery is a synchronous scan issuing the custom RDSERVICE verb until one responds; the scheme mirrors the page's own protocol.

nodes.label: CaptureAvdm() / deviceInfoAvdm() — PID capture + device info
nodes.rationale: Uses the discovered base URL plus a WADH value to request a signed PID block from the device; the response XML is what an AePS/eKYC call actually carries upstream.
nodes.norm_label: captureavdm() / deviceinfoavdm() — pid capture + device info

nodes.label: Welcome landing storyboards A/B/C
nodes.rationale: Three EPS 2.0 landing approaches built for detailed review and A/B testing; all noindex and excluded from sitemap, zero-dep motion with reduced-motion fully static.

nodes.label: Variant A — The Agent Demo (/welcome)
nodes.rationale: Pinned scrollytelling of an AI agent integrating Eko live, scoped deliberately to verification APIs only — truthful to Phase 1, zero money movement.

nodes.label: Variant B — Layered Stack (/welcome2)
nodes.rationale: Proven premium dark-SaaS arc with no pinned scrubbing — the safer build, easiest to keep fast and accessible.

nodes.label: Variant C — Terminal as Canvas (/welcome3)
nodes.rationale: Most radical and highest gimmick risk, so accessibility is handled explicitly: real text throughout, aria-hidden decorative glyphs, output pre-expanded under reduced motion.

nodes.label: Obsidian Terminal visual direction
nodes.rationale: Near-black #07090d with gold ignition accents, Inter display + JetBrains Mono — shared across all three variants and reused by the /ai hub redesign.

nodes.label: eps-backend on Vercel Pro — feasibility + migration plan
nodes.rationale: At ~20 daily users the load is absorbed by the $20 seat credit (~100x headroom); Hobby is not an option because its ToS forbids commercial use. Vercel git-push deploy would retire the whole GHCR poller + docker-compose + rollback machinery.
nodes.norm_label: eps-backend on vercel pro — feasibility + migration plan

nodes.label: SimpliBank VPN egress blocker (resolved: prod is public HTTPS)
nodes.rationale: Vercel functions egress to the public internet only; Static IPs only fix allowlisting, and real private peering is Enterprise-only. The decisive question was whether prod SimpliBank is public — it is, so the blocker is gone.
nodes.norm_label: simplibank vpn egress blocker (resolved: prod is public https)

nodes.label: Upstash Redis (in-memory KV cannot survive serverless)
nodes.rationale: Each invocation is a fresh isolate; createRedisKV already accepts rediss:// so Upstash is a drop-in with no client rewrite. node-redis forces the Node runtime, not Edge.
nodes.norm_label: upstash redis (in-memory kv cannot survive serverless)

nodes.label: buildApp() extraction + api/index.ts serverless entry
nodes.rationale: Reuses the existing createApp() factory so no HTTP layer is rewritten; memoized at module scope so warm invocations share one Redis connection. eps-backend is its own Vercel project — the repo-root vercel.json is the website.

nodes.label: /docs developer portal plan (spec-driven, 3-pane, SSG)
nodes.rationale: @scalar/api-reference is a single infinite-scroll page — it cannot give per-endpoint URLs, interleave MDX guides, or prerender — so a custom 3-pane SSG shell renders endpoint pages from api-specs.ts and Scalar is used only for try-out.

nodes.label: Try-it via Scalar modal + ClientPlugin.beforeRequest
nodes.rationale: x-pre-request script signing is dead in this api-client build (no script sandbox in the send path, and useApiClient can't forward plugins); the correct hook is beforeRequest, which runs after auth headers and before send, so signing stays our own code.

nodes.label: eko-signing.ts in-browser HMAC signing (Web Crypto)
nodes.rationale: Signs at the moment of send (a stale timestamp 403s) and deletes access_key so it is never transmitted; user-supplied UAT creds only, no bundled secrets, DEV-gated prefill so production builds never reference it.

nodes.label: Repo rename eko-eps-website → eko-eps-platform
nodes.rationale: Three axes get conflated — repo name, npm org scope, package names — and only the first changes. GitHub redirects old URLs indefinitely, so most updates are cosmetic; the one functional edit is the marketplace path in /plugin marketplace add.

nodes.label: AI-Native EPS Platform high-level plan (spine + 5 phases)
nodes.rationale: Static-first, Node backend only when truly required; per-request HMAC signing is the differentiation lever because OpenAPI can't express it and generic codegen produces broken auth.
nodes.norm_label: ai-native eps platform high-level plan (spine + 5 phases)

nodes.label: AI-agent Markdown content delivery (.md twins)
nodes.rationale: Same page content in low-noise Markdown for LLMs and coding agents, generated from the same TypeScript data as the HTML so there is no second content source. Edit the data, not the generated output.

nodes.label: vite-plugin-generate-markdown.ts
nodes.rationale: Does two jobs from one renderer set — build-time emission into dist/ via ssrLoadModule, and dev-time dynamic serving — so renderer changes are visible in both without a production build.

nodes.label: AiHint component + rel=alternate markdown discovery
nodes.rationale: A visually hidden hint helps tools that read rendered page text (rather than parsing head links) find the .md version when a human pastes a normal URL into a chat tool.

nodes.label: /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt discovery indexes
nodes.rationale: products.md is written to be sufficient standalone LLM context: boilerplate (integration steps, per-product CTAs, shared COMMON_API_FAQS) is filtered out to stay token-friendly.

nodes.label: MiniToc (Medium-style mini table of contents)
nodes.rationale: Runtime DOM scan with element refs instead of retrofitting ids or URL hashes; a MutationObserver re-scans on MDX compile/route swap. Renders null below 2 entries, which is also what makes it SSR/hydration-safe — server and first client render both produce nothing.

nodes.label: Browser-side PDF toolkit (src/lib/pdf)
nodes.rationale: Everything runs in the browser so KYC documents never leave the device until the user actually submits; nothing is fetched until a PDF operation runs.

nodes.label: compressPdf policy (image-only, NotCompressibleError)
nodes.rationale: Re-rendering pages as JPEG is a good trade for a scan and a terrible one for a real document, so any page with text or vector paths is refused. A deny-list of pdf.js operators, not an allow-list, because real scanner output routinely carries clip paths and graphics-state changes. Never returns something bigger.

nodes.label: pdf-worker / pdf-render thread split
nodes.rationale: Workers are deliberately not nested and OffscreenCanvas is avoided — pdf.js's standard configuration already gets the expensive half off the main thread without betting on browser support. pdf-render.ts is dynamic-import-only because SSG prerender runs in bare Node.

nodes.label: FileUpload multi-file combine mode
nodes.rationale: Engages only when every accepted type is an image or PDF — a zone that also takes a spreadsheet keeps single-file behaviour rather than silently dropping what it cannot fold in. One attachment passes through as itself; combining starts at two.

nodes.label: Pricing calculator (/pricing)
nodes.rationale: Three tabs with inverted semantics: verification is a COST calculator, payments/BC is an EARNINGS calculator (commissions are income to the partner), connected banking is a cost calculator. Money math runs in integer paise to avoid float drift.

nodes.label: PricingTabs forceMount (SEO-safe tabs)
nodes.rationale: All three panels stay in the prerendered HTML so every product's rates are crawlable from one URL; nothing unmounts so calculator state survives tab switches, and display:none also hides inactive tabs' fixed mobile bars.

nodes.label: Offline Excel calculator (/eps-pricing-calculator.xlsx)
nodes.rationale: Worksheets are created up-front so tab order is independent of build order (the Payments Rate Card is built first to hand over its DMT VLOOKUP range). Sheets are protected without a password — preventing accidental edits, not access control. exceljs stays out of the client bundle via ssrLoadModule + createRequire.

nodes.label: Pricing URL param scheme (tab/sel/apis/gst/pay/cb)
nodes.rationale: Every writer uses the functional setSearchParams updater and touches only its own keys, so UTM/tracking params and the other calculators' state always survive; unknown ids are dropped and garbage params never crash the page.

nodes.label: Lead attribution (tracking params, calculator context, SalesIQ identity)
nodes.rationale: Zoho SalesIQ records page URLs, so stored tracking params are re-appended after every internal navigation — attribution survives any link click without a per-link wrapper. Chat identity lives in a module store because the widget lazy-loads and rarely exists when /me resolves.
nodes.norm_label: lead attribution (tracking params, calculator context, salesiq identity)

nodes.label: generatePricingJsonLd (OfferCatalogs + FAQPage)
nodes.rationale: No Offers are emitted for DMT/AePS/BBPS commissions — they are income to the buyer, so Offer semantics would be misleading in rich results; they are covered by FAQPage entries instead.

nodes.label: Agent packages release runbook
nodes.rationale: Public npm + Packagist; the agent plugin ships straight from git main with no npm publish step. Package data/*.json is generated and gitignored so it cannot drift from src/ or leak environment values into git.

nodes.label: npm OIDC Trusted Publishing (two-phase auth)
nodes.rationale: A Trusted Publisher can only be created after the package exists on npm, so the first publish of each package needs a token and OIDC takes over afterward. OIDC needs npm ≥11.5.1, which the pinned Node 22.14.0 does not bundle — hence the explicit global npm upgrade in the job.

nodes.label: scripts/auto-release.mjs (content-fingerprint publishing)
nodes.rationale: Publishes only packages whose built output actually changed, so an unrelated monorepo change does not churn every package. Stateless — the npm registry is the source of truth, so no version-bump commit is pushed to the protected branch; a version conflict is treated as already done.

nodes.label: php-split subtree mirror → Packagist
nodes.rationale: Composer cannot install a package living in a monorepo subdirectory, so the release subtree-splits packages/sdk-php into a read-only mirror. The gitignored sdk-surface.json must be committed into the ephemeral checkout before splitting or the mirror ships without its runtime asset.

nodes.label: CI workflow isolation (php-sdk as its own status check)
nodes.rationale: Branch protection requires only the Web + JS/TS check so a PHP failure never blocks the dev → main merge that gates the npm release; the PHP job downloads the baked sdk-surface artifact because it is gitignored and never built on the PHP runner. CI never publishes.
nodes.norm_label: ci workflow isolation (php-sdk as its own status check)

nodes.label: SDK golden signing vector
nodes.rationale: Cross-language conformance fixture — base64(HMAC-SHA256(message = timestamp, key = base64(access_key))) — that every SDK core must reproduce so signing cannot drift between languages.

nodes.label: Required-param validation conformance
nodes.rationale: Validation happens BEFORE signing or sending, and fails fast sending nothing; params are baked into sdk-surface.json from the API spec so the check derives from the same source of truth.

nodes.label: Lenient type-validation conformance
nodes.rationale: Coercion-aware because the wire sends everything as strings; type-only with no format/range/enum semantics, and the regexes are intentionally narrow (no +, whitespace, trailing dot or scientific notation) and MUST be identical in JS and PHP.

nodes.label: SSG pre-rendering & React hydration rules
nodes.rationale: Each rule was a real bug; a hydration mismatch makes React discard the pre-rendered DOM and re-render from scratch on every page load. onRecoverableError logs [hydration] warnings with component stacks — check that first.

nodes.label: minifyAroundRoot (never minify the React subtree)
nodes.rationale: html-minifier's removeComments strips React's <!--$--> Suspense markers and <!-- --> text separators, and collapseWhitespace/minifyCSS rewrite text nodes and style attributes — any of these breaks hydration, so #root innerHTML stays byte-for-byte untouched.

nodes.label: FadeIn / scroll-driven reveal rules
nodes.rationale: Environment detection (CSS.supports) in render made the server emit a hidden class React then refuses to patch, locking content at opacity 0. Hidden state lives only inside keyframes with fill-mode both so an inactive view timeline degrades to visible; reveals are pinned on animationend, and JS-dependent hidden states sit inside @media (scripting: enabled).

nodes.label: Static page generation pipeline (ssg/)
nodes.rationale: ssg/routes.ts is the single source of truth and derives from the same data modules that render pages, so adding a product/industry/solution slug adds its prerendered route automatically.

nodes.label: App.tsx (lazy) / AppServer.tsx (eager) split
nodes.rationale: React.lazy is unsupported by renderToString, so the server variant keeps every page import static while the client variant code-splits. Both trees must stay structurally identical — including the Suspense boundary AppServer never actually suspends on.

nodes.label: __spa-fallback.html catch-all
nodes.rationale: Routes not in the manifest are served the original SPA shell so old URLs never break and new routes can be added incrementally; prerendered files match as exact statics before the catch-all is reached.

nodes.label: /console and /admin kept out of search (4 layers)
nodes.rationale: Layers don't stack for compliant crawlers — a bot obeying Disallow never reads the header — so the X-Robots-Tag layer exists purely for bots that ignore robots.txt and would otherwise get a plain 200 SPA shell carrying no robots meta.
nodes.norm_label: /console and /admin kept out of search (4 layers)

nodes.label: src/lib/ssr-safe.ts compatibility layer
nodes.rationale: Only a couple of browser APIs needed guarding for SSR; everything else was already inside useEffect or event handlers. ZohoSignupForm defers its iframe until near-viewport, which also removed a geolocation prompt on page load.

nodes.label: Future migration to Vike
nodes.rationale: src/entry-server.tsx is the deliberate abstraction boundary; Vike becomes worth it only for incremental rendering, streaming SSR, partial hydration, edge rendering or on-demand SSR — none of which a fully data-driven static site needs today.
