nodes.label: Vercel path rejected for production
nodes.rationale: Production SimpliBank IP-allowlists clients; Vercel's egress IPs are dynamic, so this path would need the Static IPs add-on (~$100/mo/project), erasing its cost advantage. The serverless entry (api/index.ts, vercel.json) stays in the repo unused in case the allowlist constraint lifts.

nodes.label: buildApp side-effect-free factory
nodes.rationale: config → KV → clients → sessions → Hono app, shared by both the VM entry and the serverless entry so neither path forks the wiring.

nodes.label: First-party session cookies via backend subdomain
nodes.rationale: A *.vercel.app backend is a different registrable domain from eps.eko.in, so default SameSite=Lax session cookies are not sent on cross-site XHR and auth silently breaks. Fix: host the backend on a subdomain of the frontend's domain (api.eps.eko.in). COOKIE_SAMESITE=None+Secure is the fragile alternative.
nodes.norm_label: first-party session cookies via backend subdomain
nodes.community_name: First-party session cookies via backend subdomain

nodes.label: SimpliBank IP allowlist constraint
nodes.rationale: Public HTTPS solves reachability, not allowlisting. Production SimpliBank restricts client IPs, so dynamic serverless egress is blocked; a fixed/static outbound address is mandatory.

nodes.label: Pull-based auto-deploy poller
nodes.rationale: A poller sidecar watches the :prod tag in GHCR via skopeo inspect and reconciles the running image every 30 seconds, with a health gate and automatic rollback — pull-based so the VM needs no inbound CI access.

nodes.label: Merge gate IS the deploy gate
nodes.rationale: The pull-based design has no gate other than the main merge, so branch protection (required PR, required CI status check, block force pushes, enforce for administrators) is load-bearing — a bypass is a hole straight into production.
nodes.norm_label: merge gate is the deploy gate

nodes.label: Deterministic GHCR authfile (.ghcr-auth.json)
nodes.rationale: The poller mounts a fixed path instead of ~/.docker/config.json, which is empty under sudo without -H or in systemd units where $HOME is unset. credStore caveat: if docker login used a credential helper there is no inline auth token, so skopeo gets 401 — write the base64 token explicitly.

nodes.label: HOLD sentinel file
nodes.rationale: /state/HOLD in the eps-poller-state volume pauses the poller. Set automatically on dependency fault, first-deploy image fault, or failed rollback; set manually during rollback because :prod still points at the bad digest and the poller would otherwise re-detect and redeploy it.

nodes.label: Health gate and automatic rollback
nodes.rationale: Gate polls /readyz up to 10 times with 3s delay, Redis checked in parallel. Distinguishes dependency fault (hold) from pure image fault (roll back to the previous running digest, `prev`), so no prior state is needed for rollback to work from the first deploy.

nodes.label: Seed deploy.env with the tag, not a digest
nodes.rationale: The poller pins the immutable digest on its first real deploy; seeding with the tag sidesteps multi-arch digest parsing and old-buildx --format incompatibility, which bit the first production bootstrap. Bootstrap is therefore never health-gated.
nodes.norm_label: seed deploy.env with the tag, not a digest

nodes.label: nginx must overwrite X-Real-IP
nodes.rationale: The backend's rate limiter trusts X-Real-IP for its per-client bucket, so appending rather than overwriting would let one caller spoof another caller's quota.

nodes.label: Same-origin /api rewrite over absolute backend URL
nodes.rationale: Routing /api through the site's own origin keeps session cookies first-party — no credentialed CORS, no preflight, no SameSite=None. Uses a Vercel `routes` entry (not `rewrites`) because only routes expand an env var, keeping the backend hostname out of the repo; ordering must beat the SPA catch-all. Without a real /api server, /api/me falls through to the SPA fallback and returns index.html with a 200, which once made /console render a fake signed-in user.
nodes.norm_label: same-origin /api rewrite over absolute backend url
nodes.community_name: First-party session cookies via backend subdomain

nodes.label: KV store redundancy tiers (Valkey / in-memory / Upstash)
nodes.rationale: Valkey container is the default (FOSS BSD Redis fork, same RESP, service keeps the name `redis` so REDIS_URL and compose assertions never change). In-memory degraded mode requires exactly one backend process. Upstash free tier is the managed option. The choice is deployment-time only; the backend never fails over at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: kv store redundancy tiers (valkey / in-memory / upstash)

nodes.label: KV_ENCRYPTION_KEY is a stable secret
nodes.rationale: It encrypts GitHub OAuth tokens and refresh-token claims at rest in Redis with AES-256-GCM. Rotating requires flushing rt:* and ghtoken:* and forcing re-authentication — not a routine redeploy operation.

nodes.label: eps-transact-mcp standalone production compose stack
nodes.rationale: Deployable on its own host, independent of eps-backend; co-locating on the same VM works only as a SEPARATE compose project (ports 8788 vs 8787, separate networks) so the stacks share nothing.

nodes.label: Shared eps-poller image across stacks
nodes.rationale: Same poll.sh as eps-backend, published as a shared image because a foreign VM has no repo checkout to build from. Configured per-stack via env; REDIS_REQUIRED=0 because transact has no Redis. Each stack still runs its own poller container for fault/HOLD isolation.

nodes.label: Shared-VM blast-radius resource limits
nodes.rationale: mem_limit 512m + cpus 1.0 so a leak or runaway OOM-kills only this container (dockerd restarts it) instead of taking the whole shared host down.

nodes.label: @ekoindia/eps-context-mcp (stdio documentation MCP server)
nodes.rationale: Full API bundle baked into the package so it works offline with no EPS account or credentials.

nodes.label: Tiered, lazy, secret-free tool design
nodes.rationale: Start with cheap compact list_apis/search, then call get_api only for the endpoints actually needed; same for topics and recipes. Keeps agent context small. Errors return isError with 'did you mean' suggestions.

nodes.label: debug_auth tool (known-answer test vector)
nodes.rationale: Secret-free by design, no access_key parameter ever: (1) the server is reachable anonymously over HTTP, so a key in a tool argument would travel to infrastructure that deliberately holds no secrets; (2) a tool argument lands in the caller's model context and transcript, teaching agents to read secrets out of env and paste them into chat. Instead it returns a dummy-key test vector plus ranked_causes for the 403.

nodes.label: EPS_BUNDLE_URL remote bundle override
nodes.rationale: Remote fetch capped at 5 seconds with transparent fallback to the baked bundle; get_meta reports which source is in effect (baked or remote).

nodes.label: Best-effort npm update check
nodes.rationale: One 3s-timeout registry request at startup, silent on any failure, never blocks startup; sets updateAvailable on get_meta so the agent can nudge the user. EPS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 disables it entirely.

nodes.label: Backend-only signing policy (context MCP)
nodes.rationale: get_signing_snippet emits only an algorithm template that reads the key from process.env/getenv — it never embeds a real key. This server holds no credentials and performs no signing or API calls itself.

nodes.label: @ekoindia/eps-transact-mcp (transactional MCP server)
nodes.rationale: Unlike eps-context-mcp (docs only), these tools actually call Eko, signed with real EPS credentials. Verification-category, non-financial endpoints only.

nodes.label: Registry-driven tool generation from api-specs.ts
nodes.rationale: Every tool is generated from the same single source of truth (api-specs.ts → eps.json) as the docs, SDKs, and context MCP, so tool schemas can never drift from the published API surface.

nodes.label: X-Eko-Allowed-Apis scoping header
nodes.rationale: Deliberately required because EPS calls are billed. It is a client-side guardrail out of the model's reach, NOT an authorization system — the Eko credentials remain the real boundary.

nodes.label: Stateless pass-through signer (no persistence, no body logging)
nodes.rationale: No database, cache, or session store; credentials exist only for the request lifetime. The access log records method/path/status/duration/request-id/tool name but never headers, tool arguments, or upstream responses, because verification traffic carries PAN/Aadhaar/bank data. Container binds loopback behind a reverse proxy.
nodes.norm_label: stateless pass-through signer (no persistence, no body logging)

nodes.label: MCP tool annotations for side-effecting verification tools
nodes.rationale: openWorldHint: true on all (paid external API); readOnlyHint/idempotentHint false on the genuinely side-effecting ones (₹1 penny-drop bank verification, bulk submits, OTP send/verify, DigiLocker consent URL) so hosts can gate them. Billing applies to all successful calls either way.
nodes.norm_label: mcp tool annotations for side-effecting verification tools

nodes.label: parity.copied-utils.test.ts content-hash pin
nodes.rationale: Four utils (fetchTimeout, requestId, accessLog, update-check) are hand-copied from eps-backend / eps-context-mcp; a test pins a content hash of both sides of each pair so editing either file fails the suite until the pair is diffed and reconciled.

nodes.label: Opt-in live UAT smoke test
nodes.rationale: Self-skips unless real UAT credentials are set. It is the only proof the bundle's environment URLs are live-correct, so it must run before any deploy that changes base URLs or signing.

nodes.label: EpsClient (JS)
nodes.rationale: The constructor throws if it detects a `window` global as a safety guard against shipping the access_key to a browser. initiatorId/userCode are near-constant per developer so they are set once on the client and injected as snake_case wire params.

nodes.label: Embedded endpoint catalog (sdk-surface.json)
nodes.rationale: Generated from the EPS bundle at /agent/sdk-surface.json and shipped inside the package, read at runtime so resolving a slug needs no network call.

nodes.label: EPS secret-key HMAC signing scheme
nodes.rationale: secret-key = base64(HMAC-SHA256(message = timestamp_ms, key = base64(access_key))). The HMAC key is the base64 STRING used as-is; base64-decoding it back to raw bytes before signing produces a different signature and a 403. The signature binds the request to a timestamp so it must be regenerated per call.

nodes.label: Access Key vs Developer Key
nodes.rationale: The access_key (a.k.a. auth key) is never sent on the wire — it only computes the secret-key. The developer_key is sent as a static header. Nothing secret travels in plain form.

nodes.label: SecretKeyTester browser playground
nodes.rationale: Signs entirely in-browser with the Web Crypto API so the access key is never sent to Eko or stored — safe as a scratchpad, explicitly flagged as NOT a pattern to copy into a real integration.

nodes.label: Eko response envelope (status / response_status_id / tx_status)
nodes.rationale: Status is reported at two levels: transport HTTP code and business response_status_id. A 200 OK with non-zero response_status_id is a successful call that returned a business error — always check both.

nodes.label: Financial transaction status codes (tx_status)
nodes.rationale: When tx_status is Awaited, poll the relevant status endpoint rather than retrying the debit — a retry would double-charge.

nodes.label: Integration FAQs page
nodes.rationale: Developer-facing questions only, grouped by tag via FaqList; commercial and compliance questions live on the separate /faq page.

nodes.label: Courier-not-consumer mental model for PID data
nodes.rationale: The PID block is encrypted for UIDAI and signed by the device; neither the app nor Eko's servers can decrypt it. Your code forwards it untouched. Possession of decrypted biometrics would violate the Aadhaar Act, so never decrypt, parse, log or persist Skey/Hmac/Data — read only <Resp>.
nodes.norm_label: courier-not-consumer mental model for pid data

nodes.label: UIDAI registered devices (L1 mandate)
nodes.rationale: UIDAI mandates L1 devices that sign and encrypt inside trusted hardware; L0 (host-software signing) is phased out and its captures can be rejected even when the local scan succeeds. Integration code is identical for both, so upgrading hardware does not change code.

nodes.label: RDService driver discovery on ports 11100-11120
nodes.rationale: Probe each port with the custom RDSERVICE verb over http then https; browsers allow HTTPS pages to call http://127.0.0.1 because loopback is exempt from mixed-content blocking. Find the CAPTURE interface by its id attribute, not by position, and sanitise the returned path (some drivers emit a full URL) rejecting any non-loopback host.

nodes.label: PidOptions XML configuration
nodes.rationale: Always send env="P" — Morpho rejects S/PP and Mantra fails when env is missing, and the UIDAI environment is chosen server-side anyway. Keep format="0" (XML) because many drivers return error 210 for Protobuf.

nodes.label: wadh digest binding capture to a KYC API version
nodes.rationale: base64(SHA-256(ver+ra+rc+lr+de+pfr)). Do not compute or guess it — use exactly the value the endpoint documents. Required for eKYC captures, omitted entirely for plain authentication captures. A missing or wrong wadh surfaces much later as 'Authentication Failed. Invalid Biometric data.'
nodes.norm_label: wadh digest binding capture to a kyc api version

nodes.label: qScore retry/block thresholds
nodes.rationale: Eko's production apps retry below 45 and block below 25 — a low-quality scan fails authentication at UIDAI anyway, so re-scanning early saves a round trip.

nodes.label: Android RDService integration via UIDAI Intents
nodes.rationale: Drivers are per-manufacturer Play Store apps responding to in.gov.uidai.rdservice.fp.INFO / .CAPTURE. Uses Eko's android-uidai-rdservice-manager library rather than hand-rolled Intent plumbing; the XML payloads are identical to the web flow. Mobile browsers cannot reach RDService because there is no localhost driver on a phone.
nodes.norm_label: android rdservice integration via uidai intents

nodes.label: RdServiceTester in-browser device tester
nodes.rationale: Runs the documented flow entirely in the reader's browser so integrators can verify hardware first and diff their own request log against a known-good one.

nodes.label: AePS Fingpay Biometric eKYC endpoint
nodes.rationale: Final step of a one-time-per-agent eKYC flow (Send OTP → Verify OTP → Biometric). Distinct from the daily 2FA required once per calendar day before transacting.

nodes.label: RSA Aadhaar-number encryption scheme
nodes.rationale: Base64-decode the public key, RSA-encrypt the Aadhaar number, base64-encode the result. UAT and production public keys differ. The same encrypted-Aadhaar + PID XML format is used by all AePS transaction APIs.

nodes.label: fType=2 per NPCI FIR-FMR single-PID-block guidance
nodes.rationale: Capture with fType=2, not 0. A subset of banks that have not completed FMR+FIR compliance still require fType=0, so the current bank list must be checked before going live.
nodes.norm_label: ftype=2 per npci fir-fmr single-pid-block guidance

nodes.label: AePS Fingpay Cash Withdrawal endpoint
nodes.rationale: Requires, in order: Fingpay activation, one-time eKYC, and a successful Daily KYC for the current calendar day (NPCI compliance). PID must be Data type="X" base64 XML with a DeviceInfo mc certificate and at least 35 nmPoints.

nodes.label: AePS Initiate Settlement endpoint
nodes.rationale: Settleable amount = total AePS business over the last 7 days minus settlements already made in that window. Runs Mon–Fri 10:00–17:00 IST excluding RBI holidays; max ₹2,00,000 per transaction. Declines auto-refund and reverse the balance with no manual action.

nodes.label: DMT-Fino Sender Biometric eKYC endpoint
nodes.rationale: A successful eKYC raises the sender's monthly limit from ₹5,000 to ₹25,000. Capture is client-side against an RD-service device on ports 11100–11112; on success an OTP is dispatched and Validate eKYC OTP is the next call.

nodes.label: Transaction Inquiry endpoint
nodes.rationale: Generic across all Eko financial transaction types. Look up by Eko TID as-is, or by your own reference prefixed with client_ref_id:. A timeout must never be treated as declined — inquire instead of retrying the payment, which is why sending a unique client_ref_id on every debit is load-bearing.

nodes.label: PPI DigiKhata Initiate Transaction endpoint
nodes.rationale: Treat any unexpected tx_status as initiated and follow up with an inquiry. On failure the system auto-dispatches an OTP fetched via Get Refund OTP, which acts as the customer's documented consent for the refund.

nodes.label: Get Customer Info endpoint
nodes.rationale: Branch point of a transaction flow: an enrolled customer returns an otp_ref_id to validate; response_type_id 308 means not enrolled, so proceed to Onboard Customer. Per-pipe is_registered flags decide wallet vs BC routing, which in turn affects commission.

nodes.label: Get User's Services endpoint
nodes.rationale: service_status_list[].status must not be confused with the top-level status. Re-uploading documents from DEACTIVATED moves the service to PENDING, not straight back to ACTIVATED.

nodes.label: Activate User Service endpoint
nodes.rationale: Mandatory before a user can transact on a service in production. Some services (e.g. AePS Cash Withdrawal) need extra data and have their own separate activation APIs.

nodes.label: DLT registration for a custom SMS Sender ID
nodes.rationale: Register as a Principal Entity on a telecom DLT platform, register a Sender ID under the Others/Service header category (not Promotional, and not Transactional unless it is a bank's own banking transaction), register the exact content template, then hand PE ID / Header / Header ID / Template ID to Eko during onboarding. Sender IDs are case-sensitive.
